subject: Pilot glidepath / parachute request — NovaMed
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novamed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novamed.com>, contracts@novamed.com
Date: 2028-07-03T15:02:00Z
Subject: Pilot glidepath request — contingency and downsell protections

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward with a 3-month pilot. Before we sign the SOW we have one ask from procurement and legal that could change the cadence of spend: we need a written glidepath (pilot "parachute") that allows NovaMed to exit the pilot without penalty within the first 60 days if performance or compliance criteria aren't met.

Specifically they're asking for:
- A 60-day opt-out window tied to objective KPIs in the SOW
- If we opt out, a downsell protection that preserves an onboarding credit bucket (equivalent to 30% of committed spend) to use within 12 months for a smaller footprint
- Clear language that avoids an automatic early termination fee during the pilot period; any credit calculation should be mutually agreed.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is something we can accept and, if so, what the financial mechanics look like? We attached our preferred SOW redlines for reference.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants this clarified before legal routes the PO.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Digital Programs
NovaMed Health

Attachments: NovaMed_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novamed.com>, contracts@novamed.com
Date: 2028-07-04T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot glidepath request — contingency and downsell protections

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. I looped in Marissa (legal) and Aditya (deal desk) to propose a balanced path. High-level we can offer a pilot-specific glidepath with the following guardrails: 

- 60-day opt-out window measured from the pilot start date
- If NovaMed exercises opt-out, Redwood will preserve an "onboarding credit bucket" equal to 30% of the committed pilot ARR to be used within 12 months toward future usage or a smaller subscription (no cash refunds)
- No automatic termination fee during the 60-day window; any prorations handled per the SOW credit calculation (we have a worksheet attached)
- Objective KPIs should be explicitly listed in the SOW appendix B (uptime, avg latency, integration milestone completion) — if KPIs are met, opt-out is not available for reasons of convenience

Two asks from our side to keep this safe for both parties: we need the KPIs to be mutually agreed before the pilot kickoff, and Redwood asks for a 30-day notice before applying the credit to a subsequent subscription (so we can plan capacity).

Marissa / Aditya — can you review the language and confirm whether this requires exec approval (discounting/contract variance)? If so, please escalate to Laura for clearance; the customer wants to sign this week.

Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa's summary / proposed changes (short):
- Approve a pilot-specific "parachute" clause: 60-day opt-out tied to KPI appendix; preserve a non-refundable credit bucket = 30% of committed pilot value to be applied within 12 months as a one-time concession
- We should mark that as a non-standard term (contract variance) because it affects revenue recognition and potential churn treatment — requires Deal Desk sign-off and a one-time CFO visibility note
- Financial impact: this is not a discount per se, but a contingent credit exposure. Using the attached ramp_calc the max exposed credit is ~$35k (one-time accounting exposure)

Requesting explicit approval from Laura for the contract variance and for marking this as acceptable for pilots under $150k ARR equivalents. If Laura approves, I'll update the SOW appendix and doc the variance for finance.
